result.topic_en: Latin notes on reducing a quadratic differential form (line element) to the form $dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$ via variables $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$, deriving the differential equation $f''-\kappa^2 f'/f^3=0$ and integrating it, with side calculations in the left margin.
result.transcription:
32.

Quae in formam $dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$ transit, posito:
$x+iy=\beta$ ; $x-iy=\alpha-\beta\gamma^2$ $z=\alpha\gamma$
at hae aequationes curvas reales, $\alpha=$ const, $\beta=$ const
praebere nullo modo possunt.
Casus $\psi(\alpha)=0$, $\varphi(\beta)$ non $=0$ [-ab hoc-] {+ex rei natura+} (essentialiter) non
differt. {+ab eo quem disquisivimus+}
3°. Si neque $\varphi(\beta)$ neque $\psi(\alpha)$ evanescit, effici potest,
introductis novis variabilibus $\int\frac{d\alpha}{\psi(\alpha)}$ $\int\frac{d\beta}{\varphi(\beta)}$ pro $\alpha$ et $\beta$,
ut fiat:
$\frac{\partial c}{\partial\alpha}=m$; $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta}=m$ ; $\frac{\partial c}{\partial\alpha}-\frac{\partial c}{\partial\beta}=0$
unde:
[-$c$-] $=f(\alpha+\beta)$ , $m=f'(\alpha+\beta)$
Jam sequitur ex aequatione (1,3):
$\frac{\partial b\frac{\partial a c}{\partial\beta}}{\partial\beta}=\frac{\partial b\, c\, m}{\partial\beta}$
unde habetur:
$ac=f^2\varphi(\alpha)+\psi(\alpha)$
At introducendo loco $\gamma$ variabilem $\gamma+\int\varphi(\alpha)d\alpha$ efficitur, ut $\varphi(\alpha)=0$ evadat ac proinde $ac=\psi(\alpha)$; Deinde
ex (1,2) habemus:
$\frac{f^3 f''}{f'}=-\psi(\alpha)^2$
Quum (pars altera hujus aequationis) a sola variabili $\alpha$, pars altera ab $\alpha+\beta$ pend[-eat-]et, patet, alteram
utram constanti $\kappa^2$ [-q-] aequare debere, quo pacto ad
determinandam functionem $f$ aequationem differentialem [-secundi gradus-] {+ordinis+} [-altio-] secundi ordinis obti-
nemus: {+tur+}
$f''-\frac{\kappa^2 f'}{f^3}=0$
Quibus omnibus rite perpensis aequationibus (1,1) .. (1,2) satis fieri facile perspicitur. At integrando hanc
aequationem prodit:
$2f'=\kappa_1^2-\frac{\kappa^2}{f^2}$
designante $\kappa_1$ constantem
Nunc si [-facimus-] {+ponitur+} $\alpha=x+iy$, $\beta=x-iy$ et loco variabilis
$\gamma$ introducitur nova variabilis $\gamma+i\kappa\int\frac{dx}{f^2}$ obtinemus.
$(c\,d\gamma+a\,d\alpha)^2+2m\,d\alpha\,d\beta=(f\,d\gamma+\frac{\kappa}{f}dy)^2+2f'(dx^2+dy^2)$
$=f^2d\gamma^2+2\kappa\,dy\,d\gamma+2f'dx^2+\kappa_1^2dy^2$
{+$d\xi^2$+}
Et posito:
$2f'dx^2=\frac{df^2}{2f'}=\frac{f^2df^2}{\kappa_1^2f^2-\kappa^2}=d\xi^2$
unde:
$\xi=\frac{1}{\kappa_1^2}\sqrt{\kappa_1^2f^2-\kappa^2}$ , $f^2=\kappa_1^2\xi^2+\frac{\kappa^2}{\kappa_1^2}$
Forma {+de qua agitur+} nostra quadratica abit in hanc:
$(\frac{\kappa}{\kappa_1}d\gamma+\kappa_1dy)^2+\kappa_1^2\xi^2d\gamma^2+d\xi^2$

[left margin:]
curvis realibus $\alpha=$ con, $\beta=$ cst
respondere

$d\beta=dx+idy$
$d\alpha-d\beta\gamma^2$
$-2\gamma\beta d\gamma=dx-idy$
$\gamma d\alpha+\alpha d\gamma=dz$

$d\alpha d\beta-d\beta^2\gamma^2$ $z=\beta\gamma$
$-2\gamma\beta\,d\beta d\gamma$
$+\gamma^2d\alpha^2+\alpha^2d\gamma^2+2\alpha\gamma\,d\alpha d\gamma$

$dx+idy=d\beta$
$dx-idy=d\alpha-\gamma^2d\beta-2\gamma\beta d\gamma$
$dz=\beta d\gamma+\gamma d\beta$
$d\alpha d\beta-[-\gamma^2d\beta^2-2\gamma\beta d\beta d\gamma-]$
$+\beta^2d\gamma^2+[-\gamma^2d\beta^2+2\gamma\beta d\beta d\gamma-]$

$x-iy=\alpha-\beta z$
$x-iy+\beta z=\alpha$
$x-iy+z(x+iy)=\alpha$

$a=\frac{i\kappa}{b}$

$\frac{\partial ac}{\partial\beta}=\varphi(\alpha)ff'$
$a=\frac{-i\kappa}{f}$

$(a\,d\alpha+c\,d\gamma)^2$

$\gamma'=\gamma'-\int\varphi(\alpha)d\alpha$
$d\gamma=d\gamma'-\varphi\alpha\,d\alpha$

$\gamma=\gamma'+i\kappa\int\frac{dx}{f^2}$
$d\gamma=d\gamma'+i\kappa\frac{dx}{f^2}$
$\frac{i\kappa\,dx+idy}{f}$

methods.what: Substitution showing a form transforms into the Euclidean line element
Change of variables $\int d\alpha/\psi(\alpha)$, $\int d\beta/\varphi(\beta)$ to normalize coefficients
Separation of variables: both sides equal a constant
Resulting normal form of the quadratic differential form

items.quote:
at hae aequationes curvas reales, $\alpha=$ const, $\beta=$ const
praebere nullo modo possunt.
items.english: but these equations can in no way yield real curves $\alpha=$ const, $\beta=$ const.

items.quote:
Casus $\psi(\alpha)=0$, $\varphi(\beta)$ non $=0$ [-ab hoc-] {+ex rei natura+} (essentialiter) non
differt. {+ab eo quem disquisivimus+}
items.english: The case $\psi(\alpha)=0$, $\varphi(\beta)\neq0$ does not, by the nature of the matter, differ essentially from the one we have investigated.

items.quote: Quibus omnibus rite perpensis aequationibus (1,1) .. (1,2) satis fieri facile perspicitur.
items.english: All of this having been duly weighed, it is easily seen that equations (1,1)..(1,2) are satisfied.
